instruction_bn: অনুচ্ছেদটি পড়ে সংক্ষিপ্ত প্রশ্নগুলোর উত্তর দাও (Board: short answer questions, 3×5)।

items.passage: Kazi Nazrul Islam is our national poet. He was born in 1899 in the village of Churulia in West Bengal. His childhood was full of poverty and hardship. He worked in a bakery and a tea stall in his early life. Later he joined the army. He wrote many poems, songs and stories. His poems inspired people to fight against injustice and oppression. That is why he is called the rebel poet. He died in 1976 and was buried beside the central mosque of Dhaka University.

subs.q: When and where was Nazrul born?
a: He was born in 1899 in Churulia.
subs.rule_bn: 'born in 1899 in the village of Churulia'।

subs.q: Where did he work in his early life?
a: He worked in a bakery and a tea stall.
In a bakery and a tea stall.
subs.rule_bn: 'worked in a bakery and a tea stall'।

subs.q: Why is he called the rebel poet?
a: Because his poems inspired people to fight against injustice.
subs.rule_bn: 'inspired people to fight against injustice and oppression'।

subs.q: When did he die?
Where was he buried?
a: He was buried beside the central mosque of Dhaka University.
subs.rule_bn: 'buried beside the central mosque of Dhaka University'।

items.passage: Trees are very useful to us. They give us oxygen without which we cannot live. They also give us fruits, flowers, wood and shade. Trees keep the soil firm and save us from floods. They cause rainfall and keep the air cool and fresh. Many birds and animals live on trees. But some greedy people cut down trees for money. If we destroy trees like this, the whole country will one day turn into a desert. So, we should plant more trees than we cut.

subs.q: Why can we not live without trees?
subs.rule_bn: 'give us oxygen without which we cannot live'।

subs.q: How do trees save us from floods?
subs.rule_bn: 'keep the soil firm and save us from floods'।

subs.q: Why do some people cut down trees?
a: Some greedy people cut trees for money.

subs.q: What will happen if we destroy trees?
a: The country will turn into a desert.
The country will become a desert.
subs.rule_bn: 'the whole country will one day turn into a desert'।

subs.q: What should we do about trees?
a: We should plant more trees than we cut.

items.passage: Ibrahim Cardi was a slave. He was a devoted servant of Sultan Mahmud. One day the Sultan wanted to test his servants. He gave each of them a piece of a costly diamond and ordered them to break it. All of them broke the diamond except Ibrahim Cardi. When asked why, he said that it was against his duty to destroy such a valuable thing that belonged to his master. The Sultan was very pleased with his honesty and loyalty. He made Ibrahim Cardi a high officer.

subs.q: Who was Ibrahim Cardi?
a: A devoted servant of Sultan Mahmud.

subs.q: What did the Sultan give to his servants?
a: A piece of a costly diamond.

subs.q: Why did Ibrahim Cardi not break the diamond?
a: Because it was against his duty to destroy his master's valuable thing.
subs.rule_bn: 'against his duty to destroy such a valuable thing'।

subs.q: Why was the Sultan pleased with him?
a: Because of his honesty and loyalty.

subs.q: What did the Sultan make him?
a: He made him a high officer.

items.passage: Florence Nightingale was a great nurse. She was born in 1820 in a rich family of England. From her childhood she had a great love for serving the sick. Against her family's wish, she chose nursing as her profession. During the Crimean War she went to the battlefield and served the wounded soldiers day and night. She used to move about the hospital at night with a lamp in her hand. So the soldiers lovingly called her 'the Lady with the Lamp'. She dedicated her whole life to the service of humanity.

subs.q: When and where was Florence Nightingale born?
a: She was born in 1820 in England.
subs.rule_bn: 'born in 1820 in a rich family of England'।

subs.q: What profession did she choose?
Whom did she serve during the Crimean War?
Why was she called 'the Lady with the Lamp'?
a: Because she moved about the hospital at night with a lamp.
For carrying a lamp at night.
subs.rule_bn: 'move about the hospital at night with a lamp'।

subs.q: To what did she dedicate her life?
subs.rule_bn: 'dedicated her whole life to the service of humanity'।

items.passage: The frog and the ox lived near a pond. One day the little frog saw a huge ox. Its children told the mother frog about the big animal. The mother frog was very proud. She did not believe that any animal could be bigger than herself. So she began to blow herself up to become as big as the ox. She swelled more and more and kept asking her children if she was as big as the ox. At last she blew herself up so much that she burst and died.

subs.q: What did the little frog see one day?
subs.rule_bn: 'the little frog saw a huge ox'।

subs.q: Why did the mother frog blow herself up?
a: To become as big as the ox.
To be as big as the ox.
subs.rule_bn: 'to become as big as the ox'।

subs.q: What did the mother frog keep asking?
a: Whether she was as big as the ox.
If she was as big as the ox.
subs.rule_bn: 'asking her children if she was as big as the ox'।

subs.q: What happened to the mother frog at last?
What quality of the frog is shown here?

items.passage: Physical exercise is essential for good health. It keeps our body strong and free from diseases. There are many kinds of exercise such as walking, running, swimming and playing games. Walking is the easiest and safest, and it suits people of all ages. Exercise should be taken regularly in the open air, preferably in the morning. Too much exercise is harmful. A person who takes regular exercise enjoys a sound mind in a sound body.

subs.q: Why is physical exercise essential?
a: It keeps our body strong and free from diseases.
subs.rule_bn: 'keeps our body strong and free from diseases'।

subs.q: Which exercise is the easiest and safest?
a: Walking is the easiest and safest.

subs.q: When should exercise be taken?
a: Regularly in the open air, in the morning.
In the morning in the open air.
subs.rule_bn: 'regularly in the open air, preferably in the morning'।

subs.q: What is harmful?
What does regular exercise give us?
a: A sound mind in a sound body.
subs.rule_bn: 'a sound mind in a sound body'।

items.passage: The internet has become a part of our daily life. It is a global network of computers. Through the internet we can get information on any subject within seconds. Students can learn many things and attend online classes. Businessmen can buy and sell goods online. But the internet has some bad sides too. Some people spread false news, and many young people waste their time on games. So we should use the internet wisely for our own benefit.

subs.q: What is the internet?
a: It is a global network of computers.

subs.q: What can students do through the internet?
a: Learn many things and attend online classes.
subs.rule_bn: 'learn many things and attend online classes'।

subs.q: How do some people misuse the internet?
How do many young people waste time?
How should we use the internet?

items.passage: Begum Rokeya was a great woman of Bengal. She was born in 1880 in Rangpur. In those days, girls were not allowed to get education. But Rokeya learned to read and write secretly with the help of her elder brother. She understood that education was the only way to free women from ignorance. So she opened a school for girls in Kolkata. She also wrote many books about women's rights. For her great work, she is called the pioneer of women's education.

subs.q: When and where was Begum Rokeya born?
a: She was born in 1880 in Rangpur.

subs.q: How did she learn to read and write?
a: Secretly with the help of her elder brother.
subs.rule_bn: 'learned to read and write secretly with the help of her elder brother'।

subs.q: What did she open in Kolkata?
a: She opened a school for girls.
subs.rule_bn: 'opened a school for girls in Kolkata'।

subs.q: What did she write about?
Why is she called a pioneer?
a: For her work in women's education.

items.passage: A good citizen is an asset to a country. He is aware of his rights and duties. His first duty is to obey the laws of the land. He pays taxes regularly and keeps his surroundings clean. He respects the rights and opinions of others. In times of danger, he comes forward to serve his country. The progress of a nation depends on its good citizens. So, everyone should try to be a good citizen.

subs.q: What is a good citizen to a country?
a: A good citizen is an asset.
subs.rule_bn: 'a good citizen is an asset to a country'।

subs.q: What is his first duty?
a: To obey the laws of the land.
subs.rule_bn: 'His first duty is to obey the laws'।

subs.q: What does he do besides paying taxes?
What does he do in times of danger?
a: He comes forward to serve his country.

subs.q: On what does the progress of a nation depend?

items.passage: Sheikh Mujibur Rahman is the Father of the Nation of Bangladesh. He was born in 1920 at Tungipara in Gopalganj. From his student life he took part in politics. He fought all his life for the rights of the Bengali people. On the 7th of March 1971, he delivered a historic speech at the Race Course ground. This speech inspired the whole nation to fight for freedom. Under his leadership Bangladesh won independence in 1971.

subs.q: Who is the Father of the Nation of Bangladesh?
subs.rule_bn: 'Sheikh Mujibur Rahman is the Father of the Nation'।

subs.q: When and where was he born?
a: He was born in 1920 at Tungipara.

subs.q: For what did he fight all his life?
a: For the rights of the Bengali people.
For the rights of the Bengalis.
subs.rule_bn: 'fought ... for the rights of the Bengali people'।

subs.q: When did he deliver his historic speech?
When did Bangladesh win independence?

items.passage: Punctuality is a great virtue. It means doing everything at the proper time. A punctual man values every moment of his life. He never puts off his work for the future. Great men of the world were punctual. They made the best use of their time and became successful. Those who are not punctual always fall behind and repent later. So, we should be punctual from an early age.

subs.q: What does punctuality mean?
a: Doing everything at the proper time.
Doing things at the right time.

subs.q: What does a punctual man never do?
a: He never puts off his work.

subs.q: How did great men become successful?
a: By making the best use of their time.
subs.rule_bn: 'made the best use of their time and became successful'।

subs.q: What happens to those who are not punctual?
a: They fall behind and repent later.

subs.q: From what age should we be punctual?

items.passage: The Liberation War of Bangladesh took place in 1971. On the night of 25 March, the Pakistani army suddenly attacked the innocent Bengali people. In protest, the people started a war for freedom under the leadership of Bangabandhu. Millions of people joined the war, and many gave their lives. After nine months of bloody war, Bangladesh won victory on 16 December 1971. We remember the brave freedom fighters with respect and gratitude.

subs.q: When did the Liberation War take place?
What happened on the night of 25 March?
a: The Pakistani army attacked the innocent Bengali people.

subs.q: Under whose leadership did the war start?
How long did the war last?
When did Bangladesh win victory?

items.passage: Books are our best friends. They give us both knowledge and pleasure. There are many kinds of books such as storybooks, science books and history books. A good book is like a good teacher. It never leaves us and never gets tired of teaching. Those who read good books can never feel lonely. But we should choose our books carefully, for a bad book can spoil our mind. So, we should form the habit of reading good books.

subs.q: What are our best friends?
What do books give us?
A good book is like what?
subs.rule_bn: 'A good book is like a good teacher'।

subs.q: What can a bad book do?
subs.rule_bn: 'a bad book can spoil our mind'।

subs.q: What habit should we form?
a: The habit of reading good books.
subs.rule_bn: 'form the habit of reading good books'।
